title: BlackBerry, Amazon To Develop Vehicle Data Platform
summary: BlackBerry and Amazon Web Services have partnered to develop and market IVY, a cloud-connected software platform designed to give automakers new ways to read vehicle sensor data. IVY will use machine learning to generate predictive insights, enabling new in-vehicle services and enhancing driver and passenger experiences. BlackBerry shares saw a significant jump following the announcement of this multi-year global agreement.

title: How Cloud Is Democratizing RDMA Use in the Financial Services Industry
summary: The financial services industry is seeing Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) become more accessible due to cloud migration, enabling smaller firms to leverage a technology previously exclusive to large institutions. NASDAQ's move to the cloud by 2030 highlights this trend. RDMA's high performance and low latency capabilities can be applied beyond high-frequency trading to areas like risk modeling, portfolio rebalancing, and payments, democratizing advanced computing power.

title: Amazon and Apple Are Powering a Shift Away From Intel’s Chips (Published 2020)
summary: Apple and Amazon are accelerating a shift away from Intel's chip technology by integrating their own Arm-based chips into their products. Apple recently launched Macs with its proprietary chips, while Amazon's cloud computing division is offering services powered by its Arm-based chips, boasting improved speed and cost-efficiency. This move signifies a potential redistribution of power within the computer industry, with major tech companies increasingly relying on their in-house chip designs.

title: Commercial real estate: Trends to watch in 2021
summary: The commercial real estate market in 2021 will be shaped by the lasting impacts of COVID-19 on leasing and transaction patterns, accelerating existing trends in industrial and retail sectors. While industrial real estate, driven by e-commerce, is expected to thrive with increased construction and higher rates, the office sector faces uncertainty with varied forecasts on vacancies due to work-from-home trends. Multifamily residential properties are also gaining investor interest, though downtown vacancies in some cities are attributed to factors like Airbnb conversions and a halt in immigration.

title: Kohl's taps Sephora for in-store shops to expand beauty business
summary: Kohl's has partnered with Sephora to introduce shop-in-shops within hundreds of its stores. This strategic move aims to expand Kohl's beauty business and aligns with the company's long-term vision to become a destination for active, casual, and beauty merchandise. The initiative is part of Kohl's broader effort to boost sales in its beauty category.

title: Sephora to open stores at 850 Kohl's locations by 2023
summary: Sephora plans to open shops at approximately 850 Kohl's stores by 2023, with the first 200 locations launching in fall 2021. This partnership designates Sephora as the exclusive beauty partner on Kohl's website, as Kohl's aims to significantly increase its beauty product sales. Sephora's existing partnership with J.C. Penney Co Inc will continue until its current agreement ends in 2023.

title: Why Is HP Ink Out of Stock?
summary: The article discusses why HP ink was out of stock during the COVID-19 pandemic, attributing it partly to an ethanol shortage used in disinfectants and printing inks. It analyzes how the pandemic impacted HP's business, with increased consumer PC sales offsetting declining commercial sales, while highlighting the secular decline in the printer market. The article concludes with a bleak long-term sales outlook for HP, advising caution for investors.

title: Judge throws out Trump rules limiting skilled-worker visas
summary: A federal judge in California has struck down two Trump administration rules that aimed to significantly reduce the number of H-1B visas issued to skilled foreign workers. The judge ruled that the government failed to follow proper transparency procedures and that its argument of an emergency response to COVID-19 job losses was unconvincing. This decision is seen as a significant relief for companies and current H-1B visa holders.

title: Seattle Trophy Office Tower to Change Ownership in $625M Deal
summary: Hudson Pacific Properties and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board are acquiring the 668,000-square-foot 1918 8th Ave. building in Seattle for $625 million from investors advised by J.P. Morgan Asset Management. The LEED Platinum-certified property, 98 percent leased with Amazon as the anchor tenant, is expected to close by year-end. Hudson Pacific will hold a 55 percent stake and manage leasing and construction.

title: Amazon's AWS To Leverage Israeli-Made AI Processors By Habana Labs
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) announced it will use Israeli AI processor developer Habana Labs' Gaudi accelerators. This move aims to reduce the cost of training AI datasets and lower operating expenses for customers, offering up to 40% better price-performance than current GPU-based EC2 instances for machine learning workloads. This development is seen as a significant challenge to Nvidia's dominance in the AI processing market.

title: How to use Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant with Tile
summary: This article explains how to integrate Tile trackers with Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant smart home devices. It describes the setup process for enabling voice commands to find Tile devices, allowing users to locate misplaced items more easily.

title: This chart shows how the Salesforce acquisition of Slack for $27.7 billion stacks up against tech's largest deals ever
summary: Salesforce announced its intent to acquire Slack for $27.7 billion, making it one of the largest tech acquisitions in history, surpassing Microsoft's LinkedIn purchase. This move highlights Salesforce's strategy to expand its enterprise software offerings and compete directly with Microsoft Teams. The article provides a detailed list of the 28 most expensive tech acquisitions, showcasing how Salesforce's Slack deal compares to other major transactions, from Apple's Beats acquisition to Dell's purchase of EMC.

title: Walmart+ drops free shipping minimum
summary: Walmart+ is eliminating its $35 shipping minimum for members, directly enhancing its competition with Amazon Prime. This change, effective Friday, means members will receive free next-day and two-day shipping on items shipped by Walmart regardless of order total, though grocery delivery from stores still has a minimum. Additionally, Walmart is expanding fuel discount opportunities for members, offering Sam's Club pricing at various gas stations.

title: RedZed goes live with SAP Cloud for Banking
summary: Australian mortgage lender RedZed has become the first organization globally to process mortgages using the SAP Cloud for Banking platform. This implementation is expected to facilitate RedZed's shift towards a data-driven approach, support continued growth, and improve experiences for staff, brokers, and customers. The platform provides RedZed with the scalability and flexibility needed to achieve its ambitions of increasing its loan book to $10 billion and becoming the largest provider of financial services for the self-employed in Australia.

title: WWE® SuperCard Season 7 Introduces Three-Ring Chaos with New WarGames Event
summary: WWE SuperCard Season 7 is set to introduce a new WarGames event on December 3rd, bringing a unique three-ring, three-round solo battling experience. Players will strategize their card decks to control rings, earning points to win, and can play at their own pace for various rewards. To celebrate the launch, players can claim a free pack containing an Adam Cole "Cataclysm" card and other in-game items from December 3rd to December 10th.

title: Amazon & Blackberry Partner to Accelerate Smart Car Innovation
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) and BlackBerry have announced a new partnership to advance intelligent vehicle innovation. This collaboration will focus on developing and marketing BlackBerry's IVY platform, a cloud-connected software platform designed to securely read vehicle sensor data, normalize it, and generate actionable insights both in the vehicle and in the cloud. The partnership aims to create personalized experiences for drivers and passengers, improve vehicle connectivity, and unlock new revenue streams for automakers.

title: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff: Dealmaker, publisher & political backer
summary: This article profiles Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff, highlighting his role as a prominent dealmaker in the software industry, notably with the Slack acquisition. Beyond M&A, Benioff's influence extends to owning Time Magazine, advocating for the homeless in California, and being a New York Times best-selling author. The piece underscores his diverse contributions as a tech titan and public figure.

title: Amazon Continues Investment in Nevada with Thousands of Jobs to Support Operations
summary: Amazon reinforces its commitment to Nevada by opening eight new facilities, including an 855,000 square-foot fulfillment center in North Las Vegas, creating over 2,000 new full- and part-time jobs. These roles offer competitive wages and comprehensive benefits, building on Amazon's existing 11 sites and over 10,500 employees in the state. The expansion further solidifies Amazon's operational footprint and economic contribution to Nevada.

title: FedEx Express Expands Air Network Across Asia-Pacific to Support Small Businesses for Peak
summary: FedEx Express has expanded its air network across Asia-Pacific to support small businesses during an unprecedented peak holiday season, significantly increasing flight capacity across the Pacific, to Europe, and into Australia. This expansion addresses the rapid growth of e-commerce, which is driven by shifts in consumer behavior towards online channels, accelerated by the global pandemic. FedEx is also hiring 70,000 seasonal team members and leveraging its Global Operations Control Center to ensure smooth operations during the shipping endurance race, dubbed "Shipathon."

title: Eaton Appoints Thomas B. Okray Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer
summary: Eaton has announced the appointment of Thomas B. Okray as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, effective April 1, 2021. Okray, who joins from W.W. Grainger, will succeed Richard H. Fearon, who is retiring on March 31, 2021, after 18 years of service. He will report to Craig Arnold, Eaton’s chairman and chief executive officer, and will work with Fearon to ensure a seamless transition.

title: Wayfair will close its Natick Mall store
summary: Wayfair is closing its first-ever full-service retail store at Natick Mall after approximately a year and a half of operation. An analyst deemed this move "rational" given the impact of Covid-19. The closure follows a period where the pandemic significantly influenced Wayfair's financial performance.

title: Walmart's Flipkart to spin off digital payments business
summary: Walmart-controlled Indian e-commerce company Flipkart announced its partial spin-off of PhonePe, its digital payments platform, to secure capital for growth. PhonePe will raise $700 million from existing Flipkart investors, primarily Walmart, valuing the platform at $5.5 billion, with Flipkart retaining majority ownership. This move positions PhonePe, which aims for profitability by 2022 and a public listing by 2023, to compete more effectively in India's rapidly expanding digital payments market.

title: Laredo reacts after rumors of Mall del Norte's closure go viral
summary: Rumors circulating on social media claimed that Mall del Norte in Laredo, Texas, would close on December 21 due to bankruptcy filings by its parent company and a lack of business. However, a spokesperson for the mall refuted these rumors, confirming that the mall is not closing or for sale. While the mall has been impacted by the pandemic, border restrictions, and online shopping trends, it maintains that it is operating as usual and has implemented safety measures for shoppers.

title: After Nike and Macy’s Were Hit By UPS Delivery Stoppages, What Every Retailer Needs to Do in the Critical Weeks Ahead
summary: UPS has reportedly enforced shipping restrictions on major retailers like Nike and Macy's due to stretched delivery networks caused by the surge in online shopping during the pandemic. This situation highlights the critical need for retailers to diversify delivery options, communicate shipping constraints to customers, and invest in supply chain digitization. Experts emphasize that customer loyalty is at risk if delivery expectations are not met, urging all retailers, especially smaller ones, to adapt their strategies for the holiday season and beyond.

title: Online Travel Booking Platform Market to Grow by Almost $ 205 Billion Despite Pandemic | Technavio
summary: Technavio projects that the global online travel booking platform market will grow by USD 204.81 billion during 2020-2024, despite the COVID-19 pandemic, progressing at a CAGR of almost 5%. The "packages" segment led the market in 2019, and the market is driven by increasing internet and smartphone penetration. Key players include Airbnb Inc., Booking Holdings Inc., Expedia Group Inc., and Trip.com Group Ltd.

title: FedEx’s ShopRunner acquisition provides access to e-commerce marketplace data
summary: FedEx announced its acquisition of ShopRunner, an e-commerce platform, to enhance its digital and logistics capabilities and gain access to valuable e-commerce marketplace data. The deal, subject to regulatory approval, is expected to close by the end of 2020. This acquisition will help FedEx better understand and serve the e-commerce market, especially important with the surge in online shopping due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: C3 AI Supply Network Risk
summary: C3 AI Supply Network Risk is a solution designed to empower enterprises in building resilient and agile supply networks. It offers real-time visibility, predictive agents, and AI-driven optimization to anticipate disruptions and respond effectively. The application unifies various enterprise and external data sources, applying advanced AI to detect risks and recommend actions for faster, smarter, and more strategic decisions.

title: Deutsche Bank to Move ‘Heart’ of IT Systems Into Google’s Cloud
summary: Deutsche Bank AG has finalized a cloud computing agreement with Alphabet Inc.'s Google to migrate most of its data onto Google servers, aiming to modernize its IT systems and cut costs. This long-term contract is expected to yield a cumulative return on investment of 1 billion euros for Deutsche Bank and marks a significant step for Google into the European banking cloud market. The partnership also includes joint development of new financial products, with both companies planning to sell some of this technology as white-label products.

title: Where JPMorgan Chase and Snap See Innovation’s Next Steps
summary: JPMorgan Chase and Snap shared insights on their innovation and transformation strategies at the AWS re:Invent virtual conference. JPMorgan Chase, with its massive scale and legacy, is undertaking a modernization effort involving cloud migration, AI, and data warehousing. Snap, a cloud-native company, focuses on adopting new innovations quickly for cost savings and performance improvements, while AWS CEO Andy Jassy highlighted the continued evolution of computing modes.

title: NPS acquires $2 bn US logistics portfolio with Stockbridge
summary: The National Pension Service (NPS) has partnered with Stockbridge Capital Group to acquire a $2 billion portfolio of Class A logistics centers across the US, marking the largest industrial property transaction by value since the coronavirus pandemic began. This acquisition expands NPS's real estate holdings and highlights their focus on alternative investments, particularly in the e-commerce driven logistics sector. The deal reflects a broader trend among South Korean institutional investors in targeting US and European logistics facilities, while NPS simultaneously faces challenges in exiting domestic offline store investments.

title: Kroger, other retailers see 'eye-popping profits' as workers reap little benefit
summary: A new report by the Brookings Institution reveals that supermarket chains and other food retailers saw their profits soar by an average of 39% in the first half of the year due to the pandemic, with Kroger's profits jumping 90%. Despite these "eye-popping profits," front-line workers largely reaped little benefit, as many retailers quickly ended "hero pay" and replaced it with less generous bonuses. The report highlights inequalities between worker compensation and company financial performance, prompting unions to press for the reinstatement of hazard pay amidst rising COVID-19 cases.

title: DoorDash Inc Stock Price Today | NASDAQ: DASH Live
summary: This page provides live stock information for DoorDash Inc. (NASDAQ: DASH), including its current stock price, real-time chart, key statistics, and analyst ratings. It also features recent news and analysis related to DoorDash, covering topics from regulatory challenges to insider trading and growth strategies.

title: Severna Park CEO Leads World’s Second-Fastest-Growing Company
summary: Dan Chard, a Severna Park resident, leads Medifast, which Fortune magazine ranked as the world's second-fastest-growing company. Medifast, with its Optavia coaching system, focuses on re-educating individuals on healthy lifestyles and has ambitions to expand globally and surpass $1 billion in revenue. Chard emphasizes the company's mission to help people build healthy habits, with over 90% of Optavia coaches being former clients who found success through the program.

title: Amazon to open another 1M-SF fulfillment center in Houston area
summary: Amazon plans to open a 1 million-square-foot fulfillment center in Missouri City, expanding its significant presence in the greater Houston area. This new facility will add to the company's existing logistics network in the region. The announcement was made by Amazon.com Inc.

title: Stripe: the Amazon of finance?
summary: The article discusses Stripe's ambition to become the "Amazon of finance" by expanding its financial services beyond merchant checkout APIs to a platform of platforms through its new Stripe Treasury offering. This new venture involves partnerships with banks like Goldman Sachs and Citigroup to provide checking accounts and business banking services, positioning Stripe as a potential rival to digital banks and banking-as-a-service platforms. The key focus is on enabling businesses like Shopify to offer embedded financial services to their merchants, leveraging Stripe's API layer to connect them to the banking system.

title: Greendale Mall Demolition Plan Will Get Public Hearing This Week
summary: The owner of Worcester's Greendale Mall, Finard Properties, is seeking permission to demolish the 33-year-old nearly vacant mall and replace it with a 121,000 square-foot warehouse and distribution center for Amazon. This plan will be open for public input at a virtual Worcester Planning Board meeting on December 9th. If approved, this new facility would contribute to Amazon's larger expansion in the region, which also includes new sorting facilities in Northborough and Milford, and a robotics research facility in Westborough.

title: Early success leads Kohl's, Lands’ End to expand partnership
summary: Kohl's Corp. is expanding its partnership with Lands’ End Inc. following early success. The two retailers initially announced their collaboration in March. This expansion indicates positive results from their initial arrangement.

title: Wait for Struggling GoodRx Stock to Fall Below $35
summary: GoodRx (NASDAQ: GDRX) stock, initially strong after its September 2020 IPO, has faced challenges due to market volatility and Amazon's entry into the pharmacy space. While the company operates in a high-growth sector with increasing healthcare needs and telemedicine adoption, its current valuation appears high. The article suggests waiting for the stock to fall below $35 or $33 to improve the margin of safety for long-term investors.

title: Mitch Edgeworth named president of HCA’s TriStar Health
summary: Mitch Edgeworth has been appointed president of HCA Healthcare's TriStar Health, succeeding Heather Rohan. Edgeworth is described as a values-driven executive with extensive knowledge of Middle Tennessee and other communities served by the TriStar Division.

title: Reputation
summary: The article highlights the increasing importance of corporate reputation, especially during crises like the Covid-19 pandemic, where it significantly impacts market value and stakeholder trust. It discusses how companies like Lamborghini and Ambev gained praise through authentic actions during the pandemic and examines the challenges and evolving methods of measuring reputation, as well as the financial consequences of reputational damage. The piece also emphasizes the role of transparent communication and proactive management in mitigating reputation risks and building resilience.

title: Powering Amazon’s transportation network
summary: This article highlights the individuals and partners crucial to Amazon's "middle mile" transportation network, especially during the holiday season. It introduces Isaac Issa, owner of Legacy Express Trucking, Chi Bernard, an Amazon Air Ramp Process Assistant, and Jasmin Honeywood, a Learning Ambassador at an Amazon sort center, showcasing their roles and contributions to delivering packages efficiently.

title: Threat Detection Systems Market- Featuring Amazon.com Inc., Axis Communications AB, Chemring Group Plc, Among Others to Contribute to the Market Growth | Industry Analysis, Market Trends, Opportunities, and Forecast 2024
summary: Technavio announced its latest market research report on the global threat detection systems market, projecting growth of USD 68.36 billion during 2020-2024, at a CAGR of over 13%. The report highlights increasing terrorist activities and growing demand for large-scale surveillance at public places as key market drivers. It also provides vendor analysis, segmentation by application and geography, and an overview of the impact of COVID-19.

title: AWS and ViacomCBS Expand Strategic Agreement to Transform Content Creation and Delivery
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) and ViacomCBS have expanded their strategic agreement, making AWS the preferred cloud provider for ViacomCBS's global broadcast media operations. ViacomCBS will migrate its entire broadcast footprint, including 425 linear television channels and 40 global data and media centers, to AWS to achieve greater efficiencies, cost savings, and deliver new viewing experiences. This transformation will leverage AWS's comprehensive cloud capabilities, including machine learning and media services, to automate workflows and enhance content delivery.

title: Hasbro Crowdfunders React: Company Took $10 Mil. to Create Razor Crest Toy
summary: Hasbro faced backlash from Star Wars fans who crowdfunded nearly $10 million for a Razor Crest toy, only for the ship to be destroyed in a recent episode of The Mandalorian. Many backers expressed disappointment, believing Hasbro may have known the ship's fate while collecting funds. Despite the controversy, the toy is now considered a rare collector's item.

title: Banks look at ‘explainable’ AI systems to boost consumer trust
summary: Financial institutions are investing in "explainable" artificial intelligence (AI) to address concerns about algorithmic bias and lack of transparency in automated decision-making. This technology aims to make AI decisions more traceable and understandable for auditors, regulators, and consumers, helping to build trust and mitigate issues like discrimination in loan denials. While explainable AI offers solutions to the "black box" problem, experts caution that poorly structured data can still lead to skewed outcomes, emphasizing the need for continuous fine-tuning and good governance.

title: Peloton shares briefly fall as Apple announces cheaper rival fitness service launches Dec. 14
summary: Apple announced its new digital fitness subscription service, Fitness+, will launch on December 14th at $9.99 per month, a lower price point than Peloton's base subscription. Following this news, Peloton's shares initially dropped by 2% in pre-market trading but recovered and saw a slight increase after markets opened. Apple's service integrates with its ecosystem, using Apple Watches for metrics and offering personalized recommendations, while Peloton emphasizes its hardware products like bikes and treadmills.

title: Nokia's head of global services to leave the company
summary: Sanjay Goel, Nokia's president of global services, is set to leave the company as part of a new operating model implemented under CEO Pekka Lundmark. This departure is one of several recent changes within Nokia's top management team, aimed at streamlining the Group Leadership Team to support four new business groups. Further details on the new operating model are expected to be shared in mid-December and at the Capital Markets Day in March.

title: How Brazilian Itaú Unibanco is building business sustainability on the AWS cloud
summary: Itaú Unibanco, the largest private sector bank in Brazil, is undergoing a significant digital transformation by partnering with Amazon Web Services Inc. (AWS) to migrate from a monolithic architecture to microservices on the cloud. This strategic shift aims to enhance platform flexibility, foster a customer-centric culture, and adopt agile methodologies to accelerate innovation and better meet customer demands. The CIO, Ricardo Guerra, emphasized the importance of a flexible platform to leverage new technologies and maintain a competitive edge.

title: Etsy Thrives Amid Pandemic - And It's Not Just Masks
summary: Etsy has experienced significant growth during the COVID-19 pandemic, partly due to its encouragement of sellers to produce face masks. While mask sales contributed over $600 million to gross merchandise sales by September 2020, representing more than 10% of total GMS in Q2 and Q3, the platform's overall growth was not solely dependent on masks. Even excluding mask sales, Etsy's gross merchandise sales doubled between April and September 2020 compared to the same period in 2019, highlighting broader success beyond pandemic-specific items.

title: Gartner’s Magic Quadrant for Cloud Database Management Systems
summary: Gartner's Magic Quadrant for Cloud Database Management Systems highlights 16 leading vendors in the rapidly growing cloud DBMS market, which is projected to account for 50 percent of the total DBMS market by 2023. The report categorizes vendors into Leaders, Challengers, Visionaries, and Niche Players based on their ability to execute and completeness of vision. Key players like AWS, Microsoft, Oracle, and Google are identified as leaders, with detailed strengths and weaknesses provided for each featured vendor.

title: Talk Stars: Israeli AI Startup Brings Fluency to Natural Language Understanding
summary: Onvego, an Israeli startup and NVIDIA Inception member, is enhancing natural language understanding in AI-powered conversational interfaces, moving beyond keyword limitations to understand natural speech. Their technology, already used in Israel's toll road and emergency services, aims for wider application in devices like coffee machines and elevators, and especially in call centers using NVIDIA GPUs. The company is also working on a standalone container for edge devices, leveraging NVIDIA's support to expand its reach.

title: The Grocery Dive Awards for 2020
summary: Grocery Dive announced its 2020 awards, recognizing H-E-B as Grocer of the Year for its agile pandemic response and deep understanding of shoppers. Jack Sinclair, CEO of Sprouts Farmers Market, was named Executive of the Year for his bold roadmap for the specialty chain, while Amazon received Disruptor of the Year for expanding its physical grocery footprint and streamlining shopping technology. The awards highlight companies and executives who excelled during an unusual year.

title: Variety’s Dealmakers Impact Report 2020: Top Negotiators That Have Kept Hollywood Humming
summary: This report highlights the top lawyers, financiers, executives, and entrepreneurs who have driven major deals in Hollywood throughout 2020, navigating the challenges of a pandemic and economic disruption. It showcases key transactions, client representations, and insights from these dealmakers on the evolving media landscape, including the acceleration of streaming and changes in production and financing. The article details how these individuals and firms adapted their strategies to continue shaping the entertainment industry despite unprecedented circumstances.

title: A tale of two retailers: GNC and The Vitamin Shoppe detail their year in a pandemic
summary: This article compares how GNC and The Vitamin Shoppe, two major wellness retailers, navigated the challenges of Covid-19, resulting in differing outcomes. GNC filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and was acquired by Harbin Pharmaceutical Group, while The Vitamin Shoppe, under new ownership by Franchise Group Inc., focused on digital integration, e-commerce growth, and expanding into new categories like CBD. Both companies are adapting their strategies to evolving consumer purchasing habits and focusing on wellness and beauty verticals.

title: FYI: Here Are The Best Non-Toxic And Organic Tampons On The Market
summary: This article highlights the growing popularity of non-toxic and organic tampons, addressing concerns about chemicals like bleach and dioxins found in conventional products. It features a list of the best natural and organic tampon brands on the market, such as Cora, Tampax Pure, Seventh Generation, and The Honest Company, detailing their features, materials, and benefits. The piece emphasizes the importance of choosing safer alternatives for feminine hygiene.

title: Oracle reports slow revenue growth as licensing and hardware businesses decline
summary: Oracle reported fiscal second-quarter earnings that beat analysts' expectations, with adjusted earnings of $1.06 per share on revenue of $9.80 billion, despite shares initially falling before recovering. While cloud services saw increased demand, the company's traditional licensing and hardware businesses experienced declines. Oracle's deal to become a cloud provider for TikTok in the U.S. is still pending finalization.

title: Nationwide Selects AWS as Its Preferred Cloud Provider to Deliver Digital Experiences to Customers
summary: Nationwide has selected AWS as its preferred cloud provider, expanding their relationship to accelerate digital transformation. The insurance and financial services leader is migrating over 850 business and customer-facing applications to AWS, leveraging advanced services like analytics, machine learning, and serverless technologies. This move aims to deliver more personalized recommendations and customer service, enhance internal processes, and rapidly introduce new digital services to its millions of customers.

title: Drones x Food Delivery = An Investment Duo for the Ages
summary: This article discusses the potential for drones in food delivery as a significant investment opportunity, especially given the success of companies like DoorDash. It highlights the ARK Industrial Innovation ETF (ARKQ) as a way to invest in this growing sector due to its exposure to the booming drone market. The article projects substantial growth in drone deliveries for food, estimating a dramatic increase in food-away-from-home delivery percentages by 2030, with drones handling a significant portion.

title: The dark reality behind Slack’s billion-dollar sale to Salesforce
summary: The article discusses Slack's acquisition by Salesforce for $27.7 billion, framing it as a "defensive" move rather than a success story. It argues that Slack, despite its innovative product, was unable to compete against Microsoft's bundling of Teams, highlighting a broader issue of tech giants stifling smaller innovators through monopolistic practices. The author suggests that this trend threatens consumer choice and calls for a rebalancing of the playing field against unchecked corporate power.

title: UNFI expects to renew Whole Foods contract, name new CEO early next year
summary: United Natural Foods, Inc. (UNFI) anticipates renewing its contract with Whole Foods early next year, according to Chairman and CEO Steve Spinner, who also plans to name a new CEO around the same time. The company is implementing a cost-cutting initiative, "Value Path," to save $70 million to $100 million by fiscal 2023, while facing investor anxiety over an earnings miss and revised guidance due to increased debt and capital expenditures. UNFI continues to expand by cross-selling natural and conventional goods, winning new clients like Key Food, and consolidating distribution centers, expecting long-term benefits from increased at-home consumption.

title: Zepp Z review: An excellent watch hampered by two software flaws
summary: The Zepp Z smartwatch is reviewed as a well-built device with great health tracking features and strong battery life but is hindered by poor notification handling and a lack of a third-party app ecosystem. Despite its premium hardware and responsive software, these two software flaws prevent it from being a top contender, especially when compared to competitors like the TicWatch Pro 3 and Samsung Galaxy Watch 3.

title: Costco’s revenue beats on strong food demand during pandemic
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp reported first-quarter revenue that surpassed market estimates due to increased purchases of frozen foods, liquor, and home furnishings by consumers staying home during the pandemic. Online sales saw a significant jump of 86%, supported by investments in faster delivery. The company's net income and total revenue also saw substantial increases compared to the previous year.

title: Oracle moves HQ to Austin from Calif., but don't count Nashville out
summary: Oracle Corp. is relocating its corporate headquarters from California to Austin, Texas, while also planning to expand its network of U.S. office hubs. This move comes as the tech giant had been considering Nashville since early 2019, suggesting a broader strategy beyond just one new location. The company cites a "more modern approach to work" as the reason for the relocation.

title: Government study shows taxpayers are subsidizing “starvation wages” at McDonald's, Walmart
summary: A new Government Accountability Office study, commissioned by Sen. Bernie Sanders, reveals that major corporations like Walmart and McDonald's employ large numbers of workers who rely on food stamps and Medicaid, effectively meaning taxpayers subsidize their low wages. Sanders criticized these "starvation wages" as "morally obscene," highlighting that these companies make billions in profits while failing to pay a living wage. The report, based on pre-pandemic data, points out that the issue has likely worsened and underscores the need for federal and state safety net programs.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Swimming Pools
summary: This article discusses the increasing integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) devices in swimming pools to enhance safety and prevent drownings. It highlights technologies from companies like Sightbit for lifeguard assistance and Coral Detection Systems for residential pools, and mentions the growing demand and current market penetration of these safety products.

title: European pay-TV company Sky adds Amazon Prime to its platform
summary: Sky, a European pay-TV operator owned by Comcast Corp, has announced a deal with Amazon to bring Prime Video to its platforms across Europe starting Monday. This partnership also means Sky's NOW TV and Sky Ticket apps will be available on Amazon's Fire TV devices. The collaboration will allow UK customers to watch all live Premier League soccer matches across Sky Sports, Prime Video, and BT Sport without changing devices.

title: Check Point CloudGuard is a launch partner for AWS Outposts to Enhance AWS Hybrid-Cloud Security
summary: Check Point CloudGuard has become a launch partner for AWS Outposts, enabling consistent hybrid-cloud security for customers. This integration allows organizations to deploy the same CloudGuard network security solutions on AWS Outposts as they would in AWS cloud and on-premises environments, managed through a unified console. The partnership addresses customer needs for on-premises workloads requiring low-latency, local data processing, or data residency, while maintaining consistent security policies across hybrid infrastructure.

title: PTC to acquire California company
summary: PTC, a Boston-based design and engineering software firm, announced its largest acquisition to date, reaching a deal to acquire California-based Arena Solutions for $715 million. Arena Solutions specializes in product lifecycle management software and operates on a software-as-a-service model. The article also covers other business news including Adidas's review of selling Reebok, an independent monitor for the UAW, By Chloe's bankruptcy, Burger King India's successful market debut, Amazon's unveiled "robo-taxi" from Zoox, GameStop's chaotic new console restock, the former Boeing CEO joining an electric-tractor startup, and Bed Bath & Beyond selling Cost Plus World Market.

title: Amazon’s Zoox unveils robotaxi for future ride-hailing service
summary: Amazon's self-driving subsidiary, Zoox Inc., has unveiled a fully autonomous electric robotaxi designed for future ride-hailing services. The vehicle, which lacks a steering wheel, can carry up to four passengers and run for 16 hours on a single charge. Zoox plans to launch app-based ride-hailing services in cities like San Francisco and Las Vegas, competing with companies like Uber and Lyft.

title: More parcels, fewer people: how aviation is adapting to COVID-19
summary: Airlines and leasing companies are converting passenger jets into freighters due to declining passenger demand and a boom in e-commerce amidst the pandemic. This shift is creating significant opportunities for conversion companies and helping maintenance, repair, and overhaul groups offset losses from reduced passenger flights. The trend is expected to continue as air freight demand remains strong, with a predicted 36% increase in conversions globally in 2021.

title: StorageGRID load balancer: Simplicity, performance, and advanced QoS
summary: NetApp's StorageGRID load balancer is designed to simplify object storage administration and enhance performance with advanced QoS features. It is built specifically for StorageGRID, offering easy deployment, maintenance-free operation, and traffic classifications for workload insight and resource allocation. This solution aims to make object storage more accessible and efficient for both new and experienced users, moving beyond the complexity of general-purpose load balancers.

title: HBO Max Available Directly on Comcast Xfinity Set-Tops
summary: Comcast Xfinity X1 and Flex customers can now access the HBO Max app directly through their cable boxes, simplifying the viewing experience for subscribers. This integration comes less than two weeks before the premiere of "Wonder Woman 1984" on HBO Max on Christmas Day, and all Warner Bros.'s 2021 films are also set to debut on the streaming service simultaneously with their theatrical release. The move further expands HBO Max's reach, although it notably remains unavailable on Roku devices due to ongoing distribution pact negotiations.

title: Samba TV Grows Revenue Over $100 Million Globally, Adds TiVo Data Deal 12/16/2020
summary: Samba TV, a TV data measurement company, announced it has exceeded $100 million in global revenue for 2020. The company has secured several major worldwide TV data deals this year, including agreements with Walt Disney, Comscore, and most recently, TiVo. This partnership with TiVo is expected to enhance Samba TV's targeting technology by incorporating time-shifted data from multichannel video programming distributors.

title: Amazon urges judge to set aside $10 billion cloud contract award to Microsoft
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has urged a U.S. judge to invalidate the Pentagon's $10 billion JEDI cloud computing contract award to Microsoft, alleging systematic bias and undue influence from President Trump. Amazon contends that a recent re-evaluation found AWS to be the lowest-priced bid by tens of millions of dollars, yet the contract remained with Microsoft, a decision Amazon calls "flawed and politically corrupted." A temporary halt on the deal remains in place while motions to dismiss Amazon's amended complaint are considered.

title: We Tried The Garmin Forerunner 745 - The Brand-New Version of Their Bestselling Running Watch
summary: The article reviews the new Garmin Forerunner 745, highlighting its features for runners, cyclists, and swimmers, as well as its advanced training data analysis provided by Firstbeat Analytics. It also covers new functionalities like Recovery Advisor and on-device workout suggestions. The review includes pros and cons from a resident runner's perspective and details pricing and availability.

title: 11th Amazon.com center identified for Northeast Florida
summary: Amazon is planning its 11th facility in Northeast Florida, a new 155,819-square-foot delivery station code-named DJX5, in Northwest Jacksonville's Perimeter West Industrial Park. This marks the fifth delivery station in the area, and it is designed for package sorting and delivery operations across two to three shifts. The facility is a speculative building completed by Rooker earlier this year.

title: Amazon vies for its workers to get priority access to Covid vaccine
summary: Amazon is requesting that its front-line employees, including warehouse, AWS data center, and Whole Foods workers, receive priority access to the Covid-19 vaccine. Dave Clark, Amazon's senior vice president of retail operations, sent a letter to a CDC panel emphasizing that these essential workers have been crucial during the pandemic. Other major companies in various sectors are also lobbying for their employees to be prioritized in vaccine distribution.

title: Graco Inclined Sleeper Recall Issued Due to Risk of Infant Death
summary: Federal safety officials have issued a recall for over 50,000 Graco inclined sleepers due to design defects that could lead to entrapment and suffocation in infants. This recall follows similar actions by other manufacturers like Fisher-Price and Kids II, after dozens of infant fatalities were linked to inclined sleepers. Consumers are advised to immediately stop using the recalled accessories and contact Graco for a refund.

title: Hey Presto! Teradata admits its vision is dead by hooking QueryGrid analytics platform up to rival data warehouses
summary: Teradata has updated its QueryGrid analytics platform to connect with rival cloud and on-premise data sources, including MongoDB, Databricks Delta Lake, Amazon Redshift, Google BigQuery, and notably, Snowflake, despite omitting the latter from its initial publicity. This move, facilitated by a partnership with Starburst Data and a new Presto connector, suggests Teradata is adapting its strategy to a hybrid, multi-cloud environment after a challenging year. While critics question its value proposition and potential vendor lock-in, others see it as a necessary data virtualization play to remain competitive.

title: Sony’s Crunchyroll purchase puts anime at the core of its streaming play
summary: Sony acquired Crunchyroll for $1.2 billion, positioning anime at the center of its direct-to-consumer streaming strategy to compete with giants like Netflix and Disney. This move follows Sony's aggressive anime buying spree and aims to capitalize on the rapidly growing global demand for animation, significantly boosted by the COVID-19 pandemic. The deal signals Sony's intent to become a major player in the streaming wars, leveraging the massive popularity of anime, despite prior Japanese corporate hesitations in international markets.

title: Amazon launches service that creates made-to-measure T-shirts
summary: Amazon has introduced a new service called "Made for You" that allows customers to order custom-fitted T-shirts. Shoppers provide their measurements and can personalize options such as color, neckline, and sleeve length. This initiative signifies Amazon's expansion into personalized apparel manufacturing.

title: Walmart partners with TikTok to sell merchandise while livestreaming
summary: Walmart Inc. is partnering with TikTok to host a livestream featuring fashion merchandise that viewers can purchase directly through the app. This collaboration aims to engage a younger audience and enhance Walmart's e-commerce presence, positioning it against competitors like Amazon. The initiative comes amidst Walmart's interest in investing in TikTok and a surge in its online sales during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Tis the Season for These 2 ProShares Retail ETFs: ONLN and CLIX
summary: This article discusses the investment opportunities presented by two ProShares retail ETFs, ONLN and CLIX, particularly during the holiday shopping season. ProShares Global Investment Strategist Simeon Hyman, CFA, explains the differences between the ETFs, their target investors, and how they navigate the evolving retail landscape with the accelerated shift to e-commerce due to the pandemic. The piece highlights the continued growth of online retail, the challenges for brick-and-mortar stores, and future opportunities in the sector beyond major players like Amazon.

title: Cloud recasts global data center switch market
summary: The global data center switch market is being reshaped by cloud providers and enterprise cloud makers, leading to a decline in traditional networking gear sales. White box switches, favored by large-scale cloud environments, saw significant growth while established vendors like Arista Networks, Cisco, and Juniper Networks experienced revenue drops. This shift demands that vendors reconfigure their products and software to be cloud-focused, addressing enterprise needs for independent management software and hybrid environments.

title: Graco Recalls Inclined Sleeper Accessory Sold With Playards Due To Suffocation Risk
summary: Graco has recalled inclined sleeper accessories sold with four models of its playards, affecting approximately 51,000 units, due to a suffocation risk though no incidents have been reported. This recall follows calls from a Congressional committee earlier in the year due to infant deaths linked to similar products from other manufacturers. Consumers are advised to immediately stop using the inclined sleeper accessory and contact Graco for a refund, while other sections of the playard remain safe to use.

title: Target announces Christmas Eve ordering deadline for pickup and same-day delivery services
summary: Target announced its Christmas Eve ordering deadline for same-day pickup or delivery services via Target.com or the Target app will be 5 p.m. on December 24th. This initiative aims to assist last-minute shoppers with gifts and groceries, with Target's chief marketing officer emphasizing the speed, safety, and reliability of their same-day services. Unlike many other retailers, Target offers free, contactless pickup options without an order minimum or membership, and has increased staffing and parking spots to support the holiday rush.

title: Rivian R1T is on its way to take on Tesla Cybertruck and Hummer EV
summary: The article discusses the anticipated launch of the Rivian R1T electric pickup truck, highlighting its potential to beat competitors like the Tesla Cybertruck and Hummer EV to market. It details the R1T's specifications, Rivian's significant investments and future ambitions, and the growing market for electric trucks in the U.S.

title: Make Christmas Sound Better with These 7 Sonos Speakers
summary: This article highlights 7 Sonos speakers and sound systems perfect for Christmas gifts or personal upgrades. It details various Sonos products including the budget-friendly Symfonisk, the versatile Sonos One, the portable Sonos Move, the powerful Sonos Five, the impactful Sonos Sub, and the soundbars Sonos Beam and Sonos Arc. The article also touches upon the upgraded Sonos Radio HD streaming service.

title: How to find photos on your phone? Here's how I do it.
summary: This article provides practical advice on organizing and finding photos on a smartphone, addressing a common issue for many users. The author shares his personal method, which involves using professional tools like Adobe Lightroom and various cloud storage services including Amazon Photos and SmugMug. It also highlights how others, like Kristin Metcalfe, leverage built-in features such as Apple's "Places" tool, and discusses the evolving landscape of photo storage services with Google Photos' upcoming changes.

title: Amazon closes New Jersey warehouse after rise in COVID cases
summary: Amazon has temporarily closed one of its New Jersey warehouses until December 26th due to a surge in asymptomatic COVID-19 cases. This rare move comes during the holiday shopping season and is a proactive measure taken after the company's in-house testing program identified the increase. Employees affected by the closure will be paid for their missed shifts.

title: Private-label Food and Beverage Market in US 2020-2024 - Featuring Albertsons Companies Inc., Amazon.Com Inc., Costco Wholesale Corp., Among Others to Contribute to the Market Growth
summary: The private-label food and beverage market in the US is projected to grow by USD 30.68 billion between 2020 and 2024, with a CAGR of almost 4%. This growth is primarily driven by product line extensions from private-label vendors and the premiumization of these products. Key companies contributing to this market include Albertsons Companies Inc., Amazon.com Inc., Costco Wholesale Corp., and Walmart Inc.

title: The cloud polyglot
summary: The article introduces the concept of a "cloud polyglot," referring to individuals capable of managing multiple cloud infrastructures, both on-premises and hyperscalers. It highlights the challenges of user experience fragmentation across various cloud platforms despite their similar underlying services. The author proposes NetApp ONTAP data management software and NetApp Cloud Manager as a potential solution to achieve a unified experience for managing storage and data in hybrid, multicloud environments.

title: Dogwood Therapeutics Inc Stock Price Today | NASDAQ: DWTX Live
summary: This article provides live stock price data for Dogwood Therapeutics Inc. (NASDAQ: DWTX), including its current price ($2.980), daily range, 52-week range, and key financial statistics. It also highlights analyst ratings, company health assessments, and recent news related to the company's drug development and financial activities. The company, formerly Virios Therapeutics, Inc., focuses on developing medicines for pain and fatigue-related disorders.

title: Cognizant (CTSH) Boosts Data Analytics With Inawisdom Buyout
summary: Cognizant (CTSH) has acquired Inawisdom, a UK-based consultancy specializing in AI, machine learning, and data analytics. This acquisition enhances Cognizant's digital capabilities, particularly in cloud-native AI-driven data analytics and machine learning solutions, leveraging Amazon Web Services. It is part of Cognizant's broader strategy of nine acquisitions in 2020, aimed at strengthening its presence in cloud transformation, digital engineering, and IoT, contributing to significant growth in bookings and revenue.

title: Customers Still Like to Shop in Person, Even if They Get Only to the Curb (Published 2020)
summary: Curbside pickup, initially a temporary solution for retailers during the pandemic, has quickly become a permanent and popular shopping method. It allows customers to satisfy their desire to drive to a store while also benefiting from contactless convenience. This trend indicates that the future of retail involves a hybrid approach, combining the advantages of online shopping with the appeal of physical stores.

title: Pardon the Disruption
summary: This article introduces "Pardon the Disruption," a monthly column by Lead Editor Jeff Wells for Grocery Dive. The column examines the significant forces, including competition, changing consumer demands, and the global pandemic, that are transforming the food retail industry. It aims to help companies understand and navigate these disruptions.

title: Walmart partners with FedEx on returns from home
authors: ['Kelli Dugan', 'Cox Media Group National Content Desk']
summary: Walmart has partnered with FedEx to launch a new "Carrier Pickup with FedEx" return service, allowing customers to send back online purchases from home for free. This program, announced by Linne Fulcher, Walmart's VP of customer strategy, helps address increased online sales and aims to provide a hassle-free return experience beyond the holiday season. Customers can schedule pickups, print labels, or use a QR code at FedEx locations for label printing.

title: Buyer or Seller? How Each Film Studio Tackled Dealmaking Amid the Pandemic
summary: This article examines how various film studios adapted their dealmaking strategies during the 2020 pandemic, which caused significant disruptions like production halts, theatrical window changes, and a shift towards streaming. It details key moves made by major studios such as Amazon, Apple, Disney, Lionsgate, MGM, Netflix, Paramount, Sony, Universal, and Warner Bros., including acquisitions, production adjustments, and executive changes. The report highlights each studio's unique approach to navigating the unprecedented challenges and opportunities presented by the altered entertainment landscape.

title: Inova to Build New Hospital at Landmark Mall Property
summary: Inova Health System has entered an initial agreement with the City of Alexandria to develop a new $1 billion hospital and trauma center at the former Landmark Mall site. This hospital will anchor a massive four million-square-foot redevelopment project in Alexandria's West End, transforming the unoccupied mall into a mixed-use, walkable urban village. The project also includes residential, retail, commercial, and entertainment offerings, supported by public bond financing and expected to generate substantial tax revenue.

title: Amazon Announces First Fulfillment Center in Louisiana
summary: Amazon.com, Inc. announced plans to open its first fulfillment center in Louisiana, located in Carencro, which is anticipated to launch in 2021. The new one million square-foot facility will create over 500 new, full-time jobs with industry-leading pay and comprehensive benefits. This investment marks Amazon's ongoing commitment to the state, having invested over $250 million in Louisiana from 2010-2019, creating over 750 indirect jobs.

title: Best Buy Mission Statement | Vision | Values & Culture (2025 Analysis)
summary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Best Buy's mission statement, vision statement, values, and culture. It examines how Best Buy's commitment to technological innovation, enhancing customer lives, and positive global impact drives its operations. The article also highlights the company's core values, including fostering a rewarding work environment and ethical conduct, and its guiding cultural behaviors of being human, making it real, and thinking about tomorrow.

title: Walmart (WMT) Unveils Returns Service Called Carrier Pickup by FedEx
summary: Walmart (WMT) has introduced a new return service called "Carrier Pickup by FedEx" to enhance the online shopping experience for its customers. This free service allows customers to initiate returns through the Walmart App or website and drop off packages at any FedEx Office location. The company also updated its in-store return process and continues to prioritize quick refunds, demonstrating its commitment to customer convenience amidst the growing e-commerce trend.

title: Panicking Etsy Sellers Are Afraid Of One-Star Reviews If Postal Delays Ruin Christmas Orders
summary: Etsy sellers are panicking over potential one-star reviews due to widespread USPS delays impacting Christmas deliveries. They fear customers will blame them for shipping issues outside their control, negatively affecting their livelihoods and shop ratings. Sellers feel Etsy has not adequately supported them, despite the company's claim of adjusting delivery estimates.

title: Two Electrical and Computer Engineering students land big jobs with giant companies
summary: Two Oklahoma State University Electrical and Computer Engineering Ph.D. students, Hisham Abuella and Amit Kachroo, have secured significant jobs with major companies after graduating in spring 2021. Abuella will join Qualcomm Inc. as a senior engineer on the Modem System team, while Kachroo will be an Applied Scientist II at Amazon Lab126. Both students conducted their research in the OSU Wireless Lab under Dr. Sabit Ekin and had prior summer internships with their respective companies.

title: Etsy and Shopify Buoyed as Covid-19 Boosts Online Sales
summary: E-commerce platforms Etsy and Shopify have seen significant growth during the Covid-19 pandemic as online sales surged. Both companies, which primarily serve small businesses, have experienced a substantial increase in their stock values this year. The article suggests these platforms are expected to extend their sales growth even after the pandemic subsides.

title: NetApp’s Israeli VPs leading the company’s cloud service forward
summary: Roy Alon and Assaf Levy, who joined NetApp after their startup Onaro was acquired 13 years ago, are now jointly managing NetApp's cloud activity from Israel. They have significantly grown NetApp's cloud offering, which generated $216 million in the past year, and have led acquisitions of six startups, including two Israeli companies. They discuss the growth of NetApp's cloud services, the move of data centers to the cloud, and the importance of data management and security in their acquisition strategy.

title: WEBL ETF Continues Its Climb, Rises Over 20% Past Month
summary: The Direxion Daily Dow Jones Internet Bull 3X Shares (WEBL) ETF has seen a significant rise, climbing over 20% in the past month, driven by increased internet usage due to coronavirus social distancing measures. The article highlights the fund's strong performance, trading above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, and discusses how recent stimulus packages are further supporting internet access for lower-income Americans, which could continue to benefit internet-related investments.

title: Alibaba's Only Stock Split Was Out of the Ordinary
summary: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. executed an eight-for-one stock split on July 15, 2019, to increase the number of available shares and raise capital for growth. This split coincided with a secondary listing on a Hong Kong exchange, which diluted shares but helped Alibaba secure the largest IPO listing of 2019. Despite its significance, the secondary listing caused the stock split to go largely unnoticed by American investors.

title: Time Magazine to be sold to Salesforce Billionaire Marc Benioff
summary: Marc Benioff, co-founder of Salesforce, and his wife Lynne, are purchasing Time magazine from Meredith Corp. for $190 million in cash. Benioff becomes the latest tech billionaire to acquire an iconic media brand, emphasizing journalistic integrity and a desire to preserve the publication's legacy. The Benioffs intend to keep Time's editorial independence and help it transition into the digital world while maintaining its print foundation.

title: FedEx closes on ShopRunner acquisition
summary: FedEx (NYSE: FDX) announced on Monday the completion of its acquisition of e-commerce platform ShopRunner, a move aimed at enhancing FedEx's e-commerce offerings. ShopRunner, which connects over 100 merchants to consumers and offers two-day deliveries for an annual fee, will operate as a subsidiary of FedEx Services and its new FedEx Dataworks organization. This acquisition is part of FedEx's strategy to strengthen its e-commerce capabilities as it competes with Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN), which plans to reintroduce third-party shipping services in 2021.

title: Amazon launches $2 billion Housing Equity Fund to preserve and create over 20,000 affordable homes
summary: Amazon has launched a $2 billion Housing Equity Fund to create and preserve over 20,000 affordable homes for moderate- to low-income families in Washington State’s Puget Sound region, Arlington, Virginia, and Nashville, Tennessee. The fund will provide below-market loans and grants to housing partners, public agencies, and minority-led organizations. Initial investments include significant funding for the Washington Housing Conservancy and the King County Housing Authority to safeguard affordable housing units and promote economic inclusion in these growing communities.

title: Former Delta Boeing 767s Will Become Freighters For Amazon
summary: Amazon Air has acquired three former Delta Air Lines Boeing 767-300ERs for conversion into cargo freighters. These aircraft will expand Amazon's air freight capabilities and support its growing logistics network. This move comes as Delta phases out its older 767s, providing opportunities for cargo operators to acquire and convert these planes for continued use.

title: Pfizer, AstraZeneca chosen for lab to foster Israel biotech startups
summary: Pharma giants Pfizer, AstraZeneca, Merck, Teva, along with Amazon Web Services and Israel Biotech Fund, have been selected by the Israel Innovation Authority to establish an innovation lab. The lab will focus on developing AI-based computational technologies for personalized drugs and treatments, supporting new startups in the biotech sector. This initiative aligns with Israel's "Bio-convergence Strategy" to integrate biology and engineering, fostering local entrepreneurship and leveraging expertise from global partners.

title: Intel shares rise after Third Point urges chipmaker to explore strategic alternatives as market share deteriorates
summary: Hedge fund Third Point, which recently acquired a significant stake in Intel, is urging the chipmaker's board to explore strategic alternatives due to deteriorating market share against rivals like TSMC, Samsung, and AMD. Third Point highlighted concerns about Intel's loss of manufacturing leadership and its impact on U.S. national security. Intel has stated it welcomes input from investors to enhance shareholder value.

title: Exclusive: Hedge fund Third Point urges Intel to explore deal options
summary: Activist hedge fund Third Point LLC, which has amassed a nearly $1 billion stake in Intel Corp, is urging the U.S. chipmaker to explore strategic alternatives, including whether it should keep chip design and production under one roof. Third Point CEO Daniel Loeb sent a letter to Intel Chairman Omar Ishrak, calling for immediate action to boost the company's position, address "human capital management issue," and consider divesting failed acquisitions. This push comes as Intel has lost market share to competitors like TSMC, Samsung, and AMD, and its stock has underperformed the Nasdaq Composite Index.

title: WisdomTree Computing Portfolio Has Investors on Cloud Nine
summary: Cloud computing is emerging as a premier disruptive technology, and advisors can leverage this trend for client portfolios using WisdomTree's new Disruptive Growth Model Portfolio. This portfolio targets structural growth themes, including the "MT SAAS" basket of tech companies like Microsoft and Amazon, which are seen as potential successors to FAANG stocks. The WisdomTree Cloud Computing ETF (WCLD), a top performer, is a core component, tracking an index of emerging cloud-based software companies.

title: Covid-19 Supercharged 2020's Tech Winners. What About 2021?
summary: The pandemic significantly boosted tech companies like Zoom, Shopify, and Nvidia in 2020, as they capitalized on trends such as remote work, cloud computing, video gaming, and e-commerce. While these companies saw massive gains, the article questions whether these trends will continue to drive growth as the virus recedes in 2021. The shift to cloud computing, in particular, was accelerated by shelter-in-place orders, with Zoom becoming an essential tool for virtualized offices.
